name: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex
bio: Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex (1565–1601), was an Elizabethan courtier and soldier, favourite of Queen Elizabeth I, executed for treason after his rising of 1601.
The lyric “A Wish” is traditionally attributed to him and was printed under his name in Palgrave’s The Golden Treasury (1861).

poems.title: A Wish
poems.author: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex
poems.collection: The Golden Treasury, ed. F. T. Palgrave (1861)
poems.text:
Happy were he could finish forth his fate
In some unhaunted desert, where, obscure
From all society, from love and hate
Of worldly folk, there should he sleep secure;

Then wake again, and yield God ever praise;
Content with hip, with haws, and brambleberry;
In contemplation passing still his days,
And change of holy thoughts to make him merry:

Who, when he dies, his tomb might be the bush
Where harmless robin resteth with the thrush:
          --Happy were he!
